title: Adoption of Farmbook Application for Farmers in Maeramat District, Tak Province / การยอมรับการใช้สมุดทะเบียนเกษตรกรดิจิทัลของเกษตรกร อำเภอแม่ระมาด จังหวัดตาก
author: Tiwanun Ngammuangtung; ทิวานันท์ งามเมืองตึง; Nareerut Seerasarn; นารีรัตน์ สีระสาร; Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University; Nareerut.See@stou.ac.th
category: การส่งเสริมและการผลิต
abstract: This objective of this research was to study: (1) the social and economic conditions of farmers; (2) the use of Farmbook Application by farmers; (3) the adoption of the Farmbook Application among farmers; and (4) The problems and suggestions regarding the use of the Farmbook Application by farmers.This study was a survey research methodology. The population consisted of 791 farmers in Mae Ramat Sub-district, Mae Ramat District, Tak Province, who used the Digital Farmer Registration Book in 2024. The sample size was determined using Taro Yamane’s formula with a margin of error of 0.05, resulting in a sample of 266 farmers. Simple random sampling was conducted using a lottery method based on the farmers’ names. Data were collected through interviews and analyzed using descriptive statistics including frequency, percentage, minimum, maximum, mean, standard deviation, and ranking.The results revealed that: (1) 63.90% of the farmers were female, with an average age of 50.75 years. About 39.50% had completed upper secondary education or vocational certificate level, and the average farming experience was 21.93 years. (2) 77.80% of farmers had learned or received knowledge about the use of the Farmbook Application from government officials, while 62.00% received information about it from agricultural extension officers. The most correctly answered knowledge question was that farmers can upload photos of their planting plots through the planting notification menu in the Farmbook Application. (3) The most adoption of Farmbook Application was its convenience and all the time. (4) The most significant problem in using the Farmbook Application reported by farmers was that tracking government projects and measures through the system is complicated, cumbersome, and time-consuming.
